subject: Climate & Environment
title: Vehicle-to-Grid Technology
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Vehicle-to-Grid Technology.

hook.text: The average car sits parked 95% of the time. What if it helped power the grid while waiting?

buildup.text: Electric vehicles carry large batteries — a fleet of EVs holds more energy than many power plants.

discovery.text: Vehicle-to-grid lets EVs send stored electricity back to the grid during peak demand.

twist.text: Owners get paid for the energy their parked car provides. The car earns money while you sleep.

climax.text: A million connected EVs could replace an entire natural gas peaker plant.

punchline.text: Your parked car could be the power plant of the future.

quiz.question: What does vehicle-to-grid technology allow?
options: EVs to send stored energy back to the grid

details.summary: Vehicle-to-grid technology allows electric vehicles to supply stored energy back to the power grid during peak demand. With millions of EVs plugged in daily.
details.whyItMatters: V2G turns parked electric vehicles into grid assets. If widely adopted, it could provide gigawatts of storage without building dedicated battery facilities.
takeaways: EVs can discharge stored energy back to the grid when needed
Millions of EV batteries create massive distributed storage
V2G reduces the need for dedicated grid-scale batteries

faq.question: Does V2G degrade electric vehicle batteries?
faq.answer: Frequent deep cycling could accelerate battery degradation, but smart management software limits discharge depth and cycles. Studies show that with optimized charging schedules, V2G participation can actually extend battery life by reducing time spent at high charge states.

faq.question: How much grid storage could V2G provide?
faq.answer: If 100 million EVs each offered 10 kilowatt-hours for grid services, they would collectively provide 1,000 gigawatt-hours of storage, dwarfing all existing grid batteries. Even a fraction of that would significantly improve grid flexibility and renewable integration.
